text:
maria: Running into a packaging/install footgun with the Python SDK and Poetry editable installs. Repro: in sampleapp `poetry install` then `python -c \"import redwood_sdk; import redwood_sdk.asyncio\"` -> ModuleNotFoundError: no module named redwood_sdk.asyncio. CI wheel looks fine.

sam: Hmm, could be PEP 660/editable backend. Poetry's editable mode has had cases where package discovery doesn't include subpackages if metadata is underspecified. Can you paste pyproject.toml snippet?

maria: Minimal pyproject: ```toml
[tool.poetry]
name = "redwood-sdk"
version = "0.0.0"
packages = [ { include = "redwood_sdk" } ]
[tool.poetry.dependencies]
python = "^3.8"
``` Layout is normal: `redwood_sdk/__init__.py`, `redwood_sdk/asyncio/__init__.py`, `redwood_sdk/typing/__init__.py`. `pip wheel .` contains subpackages, but poetry editable env only shows the root module sometimes.

josh: Two quick checks: 1) Are you using implicit namespace packages (PEP 420)? 2) Which Poetry version (`poetry self show`)? Older poetry/core had editable regressions.

maria: Not namespace packages; each subdir has an __init__.py. Running `pkgutil.walk_packages` in the poetry venv yields only the root package. `pip show -f redwood-sdk` also lists only `redwood_sdk/__init__.py`. `pip install -e .` works fine.

build-bot: CI job #8042 shows unrelated macos-arm wheel tag error: "ERROR: Invalid wheel tag for platform" (log: https://ci.example/8042)

sam: Short-term workarounds: - use `pip install -e .` for local editable installs; - or `poetry build && pip install dist/*.whl` to match CI. Fix: make package metadata explicit. Use the table form:```toml
[tool.poetry.packages]
include = "redwood_sdk"
```and/or add explicit include globs: `include = ["redwood_sdk/**","py.typed"]`. Also ensure `py.typed` exists and is included.

katie: I'll add a dev doc entry about editable quirks and recommend `pip install -e .` for contributors. Also propose adding a CI smoke test that runs `poetry install` and then `python -c 'import redwood_sdk.asyncio'`.

josh: Agree. Also add a tiny packaging checklist for PRs that touch layout. And ask folks to run `poetry self update` to get latest editable backend fixes.

maria: I'll open a small PR to change pyproject to explicit `[tool.poetry.packages]` and include py.typed + docs. Will link PR here when ready.

sam: And include the `pkgutil.walk_packages` snippet in the debugging checklist so others can quickly validate installed files.

katie: Thanks — I'll add the CI job after PR merges. :thumbsup:

maria: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-py/pull/2002 (explicit packages + py.typed + contributing note). Please review.

josh: Reviewing now. Thanks for the clear repro and fix plan. If anyone still sees the issue after merge, collect minimal repro steps and environment (poetry version, pip version, OS) and we can create a tiny sample repo to reproduce.
